fixes.explanation: Pethor by the Euphrates, yes. The text says Balak sent messengers to summon Balaam at Pethor, “…which is by the Euphrates in the land of his people.” (Numbers 22:5) A king sends a whole delegation to bring one man back. That's a summons you can't leave on read.

Bethel's a place in Genesis, friend, but it isn't the town in this verse. The text puts Balaam at Pethor, “…which is by the Euphrates in the land of his people.” (Numbers 22:5) Balak wants this man badly. He says, “…I know that those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed.” (Numbers 22:6) Send the messengers to the wrong town and the king's whole plan is stuck at the first turn.

Not the staff, friend. Balaam uses that on the donkey, and the LORD answers by giving her a voice. The text says, “Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth…” (Numbers 22:28) Her first words are, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?”

No storm, friend. The text doesn't mention one. The surprise is that the donkey has something to say. The text says, “Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth…” (Numbers 22:28) Picture being asked “What have I done to you…” by your own ride. I'd have no answer ready.

Sinned is right, baker. Balaam bows low and falls facedown (Numbers 22:31). The angel of the LORD asks why he has beaten his donkey, and then Balaam answers, “I have sinned…” (Numbers 22:34) He goes on, “for I did not realize that you were standing in the road to confront me.” Earlier he told the donkey he'd kill her if he had a sword (Numbers 22:29), and now he's owning up.

problems.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
The text says Balak sent messengers, but it does not say he sent no note.
It calls Bethel the 'wrong address,' using 'wrong' about the baker's answer. It also states that Bethel is a Bible place without a reference for that outside-passage fact.
The joke about filing a complaint makes light of the donkey's repeated beating.
The passage does not say that nothing in the sky changes on the road.
